review_scope: Independent read-only review of the committed runtime pipe-lifetime change
Single-instance Payload named-pipe reconnect and nested-operation paths
Synchronous native validation/Playable wait admission and connection pumping
Native cleanup handle lifetime and exact scope/ownership retention
Runtime/controller lock scope around preflight and event pumping
Actual Windows named-pipe fixture source and recorded execution evidence

observations: server::pipe::with_connection opens one PID-verified client handle and releases it when the closure returns, including closure errors.

All changed authority supervisor/status/admission/event/confirmation/cleanup transactions are short scoped. Backend HTTP calls and subsequent native transactions occur after the prior File is dropped.
The synchronous native validation and Playable loops pump admissions and connection events before each status transaction, so the MatchLobby worker does not starve those pipelines while waiting.

The host proof loop does not need an event pump: Backend P2PAuthorityReady persists the initial HOST CONNECTED proof before that poll; native event processing starts after the HOST confirmation transaction.

The remaining direct connect calls are confined to launch.rs member join and host install/login/start flows, where the same connection intentionally carries the ordered per-launch frames and no nested authority supervisor transaction runs. Dedicated registration is a separate path.

Cleanup reports host_native_cleared only after the native transaction handle has been released; failed native/backend acknowledgement retains the exact pending scope for retry. No nonce, operation sequence, cursor, or cleanup ownership regression was found.
Changed runtime lock scopes copy controller/state data before pipe or HTTP I/O. The preflight callback's controller-to-state lock is not paired with an observed state-to-controller nested lock path.

windows_named_pipe_fixtures.nature: real Windows named-pipe handles with synthetic protocol frames; no game process

limits: Read-only source review. No source/build/launch/Git mutation was performed. The Windows fixture validates single-instance handle behavior and reconnect/error release using synthetic frames; it is not evidence of Boundary native or physical multiplayer success.
